sources.title: Musopen Kickstarter recordings (2012), FLAC - orchestral, chamber, solo piano, public domain

licence.custom: Public Domain Mark 1.0 as labelled on the archive.org item (rights statement by the uploader, not by Musopen)
licence.quote: archive.org item metadata (read at https://archive.org/metadata/MusopenCollectionAsFlac): licenseurl "http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/"; description: "Musopen (www.musopen.org) is a non-profit dedicated to providing copyright free music content: music recordings, sheet music and a music textbook. This project raised money to purchase and release music to the public domain.",

sources.notes: Item MusopenCollectionAsFlac, uploaded by a third party (not by Musopen); the public-domain label is the item's own metadata, Musopen's own site could not be read (bot challenge), so provenance rests on the item text. Therefore disk-only although the label would allow more. 145 FLAC files (stored flat under music/musopen/flac/: the work and composer are in each file name, the item's folder level is dropped because the full path would pass the manifest's 120-character dest limit) (the 2012 Kickstarter set: Bach Goldberg, Beethoven, Brahms, Schubert sonatas, string quartets and others), 7.70 GB. The item describes the encoding as "FLAC ... at 32bits per sample" (item text, not measured here; the research measured 24-bit on a sampled file of a sibling item). The same recordings are also on archive.org as the single 8 GB zip musopen-lossless-dvd, which is not fetched (duplicate). Per-file hashes: each item below carries archive.org's sha1 and md5 (the fetcher only checks SHA-256 and size; the ledger records the first-seen SHA-256 to pin later). The item's own checksum list is https://archive.org/download/MusopenCollectionAsFlac/MusopenCollectionAsFlac.md5. Listening check by the owner still pending: no loudness or quality measured here.

sources.title: Musopen - The Complete Chopin Collection (Apple Lossless m4a + book PDF), CC0

licence.quote: archive.org item metadata (read at https://archive.org/metadata/musopen-chopin): licenseurl "http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/"; item title "Musopen - The Complete Chopin Collection"; uploader address at musopen.org.

sources.notes: Uploaded from a musopen.org address (the rights holder's own upload), CC0 by the item metadata. Fetched: the Apple Lossless (.m4a) audio files and the PDF book "The Music of Frederic Chopin"; not fetched: the MP3, Ogg and analysis files of the same item. Apple Lossless is lossless but not FLAC: players and ffmpeg read it, the editor must be able to decode m4a/alac. Per-file hashes: sha1 and md5 from archive.org are in each item's notes. Not committed to the repository in practice because of size, although the licence allows it.

sources.title: FSD50K: 51,197 Freesound clips (0.3-30 s, 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono PCM) in 200 sound-event classes

licence.custom: Per-clip Creative Commons licences (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-NC, CC Sampling+); dataset as a whole CC BY 4.0; commercial use of the dataset requires contacting the authors
licence.quote: Zenodo record 4060432 description: "All audio clips in FSD50K are released under Creative Commons (CC) licenses. Each clip has its own license as defined by the clip uploader in Freesound, some of them requiring attribution to their original authors and some forbidding further commercial reuse." Development set: "CC0: 14,959 CC-BY: 20,017 CC-BY-NC: 4616 CC Sampling+: 1374"; evaluation set: "CC0: 4914 CC-BY: 3489 CC-BY-NC: 1425 CC Sampling+: 403". "FSD50K is released under CC-BY" as a whole (FSD50K.doc/LICENSE-DATASET) and "If you'd like to use FSD50K for commercial purposes, please contact Eduardo Fonseca and Frederic Font".

sources.credit: Sound by <Freesound uploader> (<clip licence>), from FSD50K (Fonseca, Plakal, Font, Ellis, Serra), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4060432 - uploader and licence taken from the clip's entry in FSD50K.metadata
sources.notes: MIXED PER-CLIP LICENCES, including CC BY-NC (6,041 of 51,197 clips, about 12%) and CC Sampling+, and the authors ask to be contacted for commercial use: so the whole set is disk-only, personal-only, never committed, never inside a project archive that leaves the owner. THE EDITOR MUST READ THE PER-CLIP LICENCE FROM THE DATASET METADATA (FSD50K.metadata/dev_clips_info_FSD50K.json and eval_clips_info_FSD50K.json: uploader, title and licence per clip) BEFORE OFFERING A CLIP, offer only CC0 and CC BY clips in anything shared, and put the credit line (the line above is a template: the real uploader, title and licence come from that file) into every shared video that uses a CC BY clip. The credit line is composed here from the record's authors and DOI, not the publisher's wording. Raw Freesound sounds can attract Content ID claims (research section 8). SPLIT ZIPS: the audio is published as multi-part zips (FSD50K.dev_audio.z01..z05 + FSD50K.dev_audio.zip, FSD50K.eval_audio.z01 + FSD50K.eval_audio.zip). The fetcher cannot join them; all parts are fetched as plain files into one folder (sounds/fsd50k) and joining needs 7-Zip on the laptop (not installed): "7z x FSD50K.dev_audio.zip" and "7z x FSD50K.eval_audio.zip" with all parts in the same folder. Download size 24.7 GB; unpacked about the same again, so 50 GB of disk is needed until the owner deletes the parts after unpacking (count 24.7 GB as kept if the parts are kept). Zenodo publishes md5 only; each item's notes carry the publisher's md5, the fetcher records the first-seen SHA-256 (only the three small files have a SHA-256 here, computed on 2026-11-25).

sources.credit: Loop by <Freesound uploader> (<loop licence>), from the Freesound Loop Dataset (Ramires et al., ISMIR 2020), https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3967852 - uploader and licence taken from FSL10K/metadata.json
sources.notes: MIXED PER-LOOP LICENCES: the README says only that every sound has "some kind of Creative Commons license" and the per-sound licence is in FSL10K/metadata.json inside the zip; the licence mix was NOT read (the zip was not downloaded), so the set is treated like FSD50K: disk-only, personal-only (it may contain CC BY-NC loops), and the editor must read each loop's licence from FSL10K/metadata.json before offering it and offer only CC0/CC BY ones in anything shared. Credit line is a template composed here, not the publisher's wording. Zip is 8.84 GB (single file, zip64 is read by the fetcher); Zenodo md5 c260a1203a82c1dda80ec1de75e5e23f; unpacked size not measured (budget reservation counts it as 0). Small files below have SHA-256 computed on 2026-11-25.

sources.title: Incompetech (Kevin MacLeod): 1443 royalty-free MP3 tracks, CC BY 4.0

licence.quote: Music FAQ: "for YouTube videos? Yes, AND you can monetize the videos. Be sure to credit me." Crediting: "Title Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) / Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0 / https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ ... It is important that you replace the word Title with the Actual Title of the piece that you are using!" and "Is this music Copyright Free? No. All of this music is copyrighted."

sources.credit:
Title Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)
Licensed under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
sources.notes: The credit line is the publisher's own three-line text with the word "Title" standing for the track title, which the editor must substitute (title per file: pieces.json, field "title", matched by "filename"; the format has one credit per source, not per item). For YouTube the credit must be in the video DESCRIPTION text (the FAQ says so; the credit inside the video is not read by Content ID): research section 8 trap 2. File list taken from the official catalogue file pieces.json on 2026-11-25: 1443 tracks, 11.40 GB; bytes are the Content-Length the server answered to a HEAD request on 2026-11-25 (one request per file at one per half second). The server gives only ETag/Last-Modified, no hash: files are unpinned (first-seen SHA-256 in the ledger), and a track that the publisher re-uploads later will fail the size check - run the manifest again after refreshing. MP3 only (44.1 kHz; 256-320 kbps in the two files the research measured; loudness varies by track, the research measured -12.3 and -20.2 LUFS: normalise at playback). Only the free MP3 route is used; the paid USD 38 bundle (stems, the credit PDF) is not. 1,443 tracks, a few of which are public-domain classical pieces performed by the artist: the licence of the recording is still CC BY.

items.notes: Live catalogue file, changes whenever tracks are added: no size or hash pinned (first-seen SHA-256 goes to the ledger).
